item.description: A state record has fallen, Mid-Illini Conference goes 3-1, and El Paso-Gridley looks impressive — plus, we preview the upcoming second round. Here are some takeaways from Friday, Oct. 30 first-round games of the Illinois High School Association football playoffs around the Peoria area: 88-84? Imagine scoring 84 points in a football playoff game. At home. And losing. That's exactly what just happened Friday, Oct. 30 in an afternoon Class 6A first-round playoff game that produced an IHSA state record for most points in a playoff game where both teams score, and took two fields to finish. No. 9 seed Quincy rolled into town and beat No. 8 Chicago Goode, 88-84. The 172 points were a state record for most points combined in an IHSA playoff game, surpassing the 166 posted in a Springfield High 94-72 win over Rock Island on Oct. 29, 2021. The record brought back some Peoria-area football memories of an 82-80 overtime regular-season game in which Peoria High beat Peoria Notre Dame on Sept. 15, 2017 at Peoria Stadium. That is the state record for most points in a regular-season game in which both teams scored. As for Quincy vs Goode, the game started at 3 p.m. and was played on a field with no lights. Game had to be suspended because of darkness with 3:42 left in regulation while they searched for a field with lights. They ended up at Chicago Englewood's field and finished it out there. Mid-Illini wins a trio of games The Mid-Illini Conference boasted a 3-1 record after the opening night of first-round action. Morton, Pekin and Metamora all pulled out victories, while Washington saw its season come to an end. The Redbirds, however, had the most dramatic win, knocking off fifth-seed Breese Central 21-20. Metamora got a 27-yard, go-ahead TD from Brayden Cox with 54.9 seconds left. Jeeter Schweigert then found Elijah Edwards for a two-point conversion and the win. Cox then sealed the victory with an interception on BC's potential game-winning drive. Pekin picked up a 50-6 home win over Harvey Thornton, utilizing the services of freshman Rowen McKnight at starting quarterback. The normal QB1 Matthew Stropes III was sidelined with a broken hand. Dunlap gives the M-I a chance for a fourth second-round participant when it hosts LaGrange Park Nazareth Academy at 1:30 p.m. Saturday, Oct. 31. All-state quarterback Owen Adams threw for 174 yards on 12-of-17 passing, finding Braden Gibson (22 yards) and Aaden Adams (10 yards) for TDs. Aaden Adams added three rushing TDs for EP-G, which produced 328 yards of total offense (104 rushing, 224 passing). item.title: “This Is an Epidemic at This Point”: NBA Fans Frustrated as Ja Morant Becomes Latest Star Hit by Injury Bug
item.description: Ja Morant © Trail Blazers/X As if the start of the 2026-27 season couldn’t be more frustrating, another star player is already set to miss time with an injury. On Friday night, the Portland Trail Blazers announced that Ja Morant will miss at least four weeks with a Grade 2 left hamstring strain. The All-Star guard is the latest name on a growing list of players dealing with early-season injuries. He joins stars like Anthony Edwards, Jalen Williams, Tyrese Haliburton, Kawhi Leonard, Paolo Banchero and Ben Simmons on the shelf. Morant suffered the injury during Thursday’s 124-103 loss to his former team, the Memphis Grizzlies. He appeared to hurt his left hamstring while going for an offensive rebound midway through the fourth quarter. He tried to play through the discomfort but eventually left the game and did not return. Fans were frustrated to see another name added to the league’s growing injury list and had plenty to say on social media. Here’s a look at some of the reactions. “C’mon man, this is an epidemic at this point,” a fan said on X. The injury is a major blow for both Morant and the team. He had just started getting comfortable with his new team, and Portland will now be without a key guard and a locker-room leader for quite some time. Morant played 23 minutes against Memphis, scoring 14 points on 6-of-14 shooting. It was also the Trail Blazers’ first loss of the season after starting with a three-game winning streak. What Does Ja Morant’s Injury Mean for Scoot Henderson? It’s never good to see a player go down, but in the cutthroat NBA, every opportunity counts. Losing Morant for at least four weeks is bad news for Portland, but it could quietly benefit a certain player: Scoot Henderson. The fourth-year guard has seen his role shrink significantly since Morant arrived. With him now sidelined for quite some time, Henderson could get more opportunities to either solidify his place in Portland’s lineup or showcase himself for a potential trade. It won’t be easy, though. Henderson has been coming off the bench, averaging 7.5 points in 18.8 minutes per game, down from 24.9 minutes last season. In his most recent game against Memphis, he played just 19 minutes and scored nine points on 3-of-8 shooting. He also went 1-of-5 from beyond the arc, taking his 3-point shooting to just 2-of-17 through four games. Henderson’s problem is that, whether Morant is in the lineup or not, he hasn’t been able to seize the moment and establish himself as a reliable day-to-day option. That’s why many fans believe he needs a fresh start with another team. It will be interesting to see how much he can make of the opportunity over the next four weeks. item.title: Brewers’ 750,000 fan World Series parade attendance makes Milwaukee history
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images Brewers’ 750,000 fan World Series parade attendance makes Milwaukee history appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Milwaukee turned out in historic numbers to celebrate the Brewers’ first World Series championship , with more than 750,000 fans filling the city’s streets and festival grounds for Friday’s parade and rally. According to the Milwaukee Police Department, estimated attendance surpassed three-quarters of a million, potentially making it the largest crowd ever gathered for a single-day event in Wisconsin. The turnout was remarkable even by championship standards, drawing nearly one-and-a-half times Milwaukee’s population. The celebration brought together fans from across the state, with generations of Brewers supporters filling downtown streets and cheering from parking garages and office windows. The excitement reached beyond the parade route, as Milwaukee Public Schools canceled classes to allow the community to take part in the historic celebration. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The players and organization also embraced the occasion. President of baseball operations Matt Arnold joined the festivities with a beer in hand, while Hall of Famer Rollie Fingers praised Aaron Ashby and the team’s bullpen. World Series MVP William Contreras delivered a message directly to the supporters, saying, “We did it for you guys, for the city.” The celebration also carried a special place in Milwaukee’s baseball history. In 1982, Brewers fans held a parade to honor the team despite its World Series loss to the St. Louis Cardinals. This time, however, the city had a championship to celebrate. More than four decades later, Milwaukee finally welcomed its long-awaited title parade. The massive turnout reflected the significance of the achievement, bringing generations of fans together to celebrate a moment the franchise and its supporters had waited years to experience. item.title: What Josh Kushner 'assured' Mark Walter in a private meeting before agreeing $12.5B Lakers sale
item.description: Photo by Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images The sale of the Los Angeles Lakers looks like it is finally about to be completed. It has been over two months now since news emerged that Josh Kushner and Bob Iger would be purchasing a majority stake in the franchise. Negotiations have dragged on, but it looks like Kushner and Mark Walter have all but finalised the transaction following a private meeting this week. Josh Kushner ‘assured’ Mark Walter he has the funds to complete $12.5B Lakers purchase There have been some wild stories emerging that Kushner may not actually have the money to complete the purchase of the Los Angeles Lakers. Reports in August claimed that talks were ongoing for a $12 billion sale of the franchise, but there was no public movement on that front over the last two months. However, ESPN have now revealed that Kushner and Walter held a meeting at the latter’s residence in Florida on Thursday, and the outcome is positive. It has been claimed that the two parties have agreed on all outstanding terms of the sale, and it is now set to be completed at a valuation of $12.5 billion. A formal agreement is set to be signed soon, and once that is done, the deal will be reviewed by the NBA, which will do a deep dive into the financing and ownership structure. That may take some time. However, during the meeting, the report says that Kushner ‘assured’ Walter that ‘he has raised all the money necessary to complete the sale’ of the Lakers. It now remains to be seen how soon the deal can be completed between the two parties and then ratified by the NBA.

item.title: Parker Robinson sets Neville football's passing record as Tigers clinch district
item.description: MONROE — Parker Robinson has Neville High School’s all-time leading passing record with 6,789 yards. The senior quarterback and Louisiana-Monroe commit took the record, which belonged for over two decades to Robert Lane, during a scoring drive in which he totaled his fourth touchdown of the night, a 12-yard strike to sophomore Deuntra Schneatte, in the Tigers’ District 2-4A matchup against Tioga. Robinson and Schneatte also hooked up for an 80-yard score on Neville’s first offensive play of the game. After making back-to-back semifinals in Division I nonselect, Neville hasn’t missed a beat in its move to D-II nonselect this fall. It clinched the District 2-4A title following its 45-14 victory against Tioga on Friday, Oct. 30, at Mickey McCarty Field. “We’ve had a lot of ups and downs with this team, but I think the thing that separates us is just our chemistry and how close we are,” Robinson said. “We really are family. We fight like brothers; we compete like brothers every day. A good or bad play, we keep level-headed; we complement each other. item.description: BOSTON — Boston Celtics fans didn't roll out the red carpet for Paul George when he was traded to Beantown in July. Many were still upset by the shock of losing former Celtics star Jaylen Brown in the deal and getting back a 36-year-old wing (along with a few draft picks) from the rival Philadelphia 76ers. And while that consternation was justified, George has shown that he was much more than an afterthought in the stunning offseason move. Through five games, the nine-time All-Star is averaging over 22 points per outing while shooting about 44 percent from 3-point land. The Celtics posted a 4-1 record in that span and most recently beat the Chicago Bulls on Friday night in a 125-111 victory at TD Garden. George logged 18 points, 8 assists, 6 rebounds, and a game-high 3 steals in 27 minutes of play during the NBA Cup group-play opener. The fact that the future Hall of Famer can score in droves isn't a shock. The Celtics witnessed George's offensive prowess just last postseason when he was still on the Sixers. He torched them in multiple playoff games and shot a blistering 55 percent from deep in the first round. Where George has surprised is on defense. He's averaged 5.8 deflections per game — the most of any player in the NBA so far — and impressed his new teammates on that all-important end of the floor. “He’s really a complete player," Celtics point guard Payton Pritchard told Celtics Wire. "Obviously, I knew offensively he's gifted and can score on all three levels and make plays, but his defense is phenomenal. And I didn't know how good it was until I saw it up close.” It's early in the season and the Celtics haven't faced the most formidable competition as of late (including recent wins versus the winless Brooklyn Nets and struggling Bulls), yet George's productivity on both sides of the ball remains a promising sign. “He gets his hands on a lot of balls and is in passing lanes," Pritchard continued at the podium. item.description: Motorsport photo Jorge Martin has admitted that his chances of winning the 2026 MotoGP title are over following his withdrawal from the Malaysian Grand Prix, although he remains determined to fight until the end of the season. The factory Aprilia rider attempted to race at Sepang just a week after breaking his right wrist in the Phillip Island sprint, but was ultimately forced to withdraw from the weekend just before the start of qualifying. Having already dropped to second in the championship in Australia, 10 points behind Marc Marquez , Martin is expected to lose further ground to his Ducati rival across the two points-paying races at Sepang. With only three rounds remaining after Malaysia, the Spaniard has conceded that he considers his title challenge effectively over. “For sure, the championship is there. I think now I don't have to think about the championship. Maybe I can win it, but for me it's already lost.” However, the Spaniard remains keen to put up a fight in the closing stages of the season for the sake of Aprilia, which is fighting for its maiden titles in MotoGP. “For sure, I will fight till the end,” he vowed. “Not only for me, because at the end of the day I'm already champion [in 2024], but for my team, for my people I will fight till the end.” Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team While the non-displaced radius fracture that Martin suffered usually takes several weeks to heal, the Spaniard underwent an extensive recovery programme in a bid to race in Malaysia. But after returning to the track in FP3 to assess his conditions, Martin ultimately decided that he wasn’t fit enough to continue with the weekend. The 28-year-old is now hoping to recover sufficiently in order to take part in next week’s Qatar Grand Prix. “I tried, I tried my best, I tried to ride, but the process of healing is still early,” he said. “The healing is going really fast, but not enough to be efficient on the bike. I felt that I could ride with almost no pain, but for maybe one lap. After that, I started to have a lot of pain, I couldn't be constant. So watching the lap times and my performance, we decided to stop, to try to wait. “Also, we have Qatar next week and my target is to go there. item.description: CHILLICOTHE — Coming into a first-round playoff matchup with Cincinnati Northwest, Unioto knew it had to do two things well. The Shermans identified two priorities in their game plan: control time of possession and limit Northwest's ability to produce explosive plays. Defensively, the Shermans made Northwest work for everything, forcing three turnovers while surrendering just 193 yards of total offense. The result was a 17-0 win over the Knights Friday night, Oct. 30, giving the program its third playoff victory and second consecutive trip to Week 12. “With the way we game-planned this, we knew that Northwest was more than capable of hitting us with some big plays,” Unioto head coach Matt Hoops said. “But we weren’t convinced they could keep the ball and sustain 80-yard drives. Wilson helped the Shermans control the clock, running 31 times for 156 yards and two touchdowns. “Yusef was the man tonight,” Hoops said. “He showed up and proved what he was capable of doing. item.description: Angel Reese and Gabby Williams © X/@AtlantaDream and @valkyries The 2026 WNBA Finals will come down to a Game 7 for the first time as the Golden State Valkyries take on the Atlanta Dream in a decisive Saturday night matchup. The series returns to Chase Center in San Francisco after the Dream’s 80-69 Game 6 win on Thursday. Ahead of the winner-take-all finale, ESPN analyst Monica McNutt offered her prediction during Friday’s episode of First Take, giving the Valkyries a slight edge while identifying 75 points as the magic number that could decide the championship. “This series has been incredible. I’m giving a slight advantage to the Valkyries going back home,” McNutt said. “But I will say I think the magic number in Game 7 is going to be 75 points. The Valkyries have a tremendous record, something like 22-2 when they hold teams under 70 points. In fact, they held teams to around 72 during the course of the regular season.” Golden State is quite used to playing tight games. The Valkyries’ brand of suffocating defense has been a major factor throughout the series, with all their wins coming by narrow margins. Meanwhile, Atlanta has won when it has scored more than 75 points, making that mark particularly important heading into Game 7. McNutt also credited Dream head coach Karl Smesko for recognizing the importance of pace and making the necessary adjustments that helped Atlanta win Game 6. She believes the Dream have enough firepower to challenge Golden State if they can maintain that approach. “And obviously what you saw in Game 6, and it was a great timeout sound from Karl Smesko saying the pace is where the Dream’s strength lies. They’re getting up and down the floor. They have an offense and defense that was top five in both offensive and defensive rating through the course of the regular season. So when you look at this group, there’s a little bit more in the arsenal in terms of their ability to score with ease. If they are getting up and down the floor and can score over 75 points, I think they might steal this one back out in Golden State.” That’s exactly what happened in Game 6: Atlanta started strong and took a 32-15 lead in the first quarter. The Dream led by as many as 25 points, and although the Valkyries tried to fight back, they could not close the gap. item.title: Joc Pederson Declines $18.5M Option, Hits Free Agency
item.description: Raymond Carlin III-Imagn Images Joc Pederson is no longer a Texas Ranger. The beloved 2021 World Series champion for the Atlanta Braves has officially entered free agency after turning down a massive $18.5 million mutual option, according to Heavy.com . This move leaves a key spot open in the designated hitter role for the upcoming season. Per reports, the decision was made on Friday, opening the door for teams to make their pitch. The 34-year-old slugger is coming off a season where he proved he still has plenty of power left in his bat. He hit 26 home runs in 136 games last year and posted an OPS+ of 134. That number shows he was well above the league average. It is a strong resume for a player looking to sign his next big deal. The Texas Rangers will likely try to keep him, but the Braves have a clear need to fill. item.description: JENSEN BEACH — The Jensen Beach High School football team chanted "Jensen County" in unison after the game while gathered on a wet and muddy field at the Birdcage. For the previous two years, the Falcons walked off the field after their regular-season finale having to accept the bitter taste of defeat against their biggest rival. Their loss last season to Martin County High was particularly excruciating after they allowed only one touchdown but still relinquished the lead in the game's late stages. But thanks to an explosive midgame stretch, Jensen Beach can once again call itself the king of the county. The Falcons erupted for 35 points in less than a 12-minute span en route to demolishing the Tigers 42-0 and regaining the Fergie Ferguson Trophy on Friday night at Jensen Beach High School. "It all goes back to offseason conditioning, mindset, working hard, creating a goal for yourself and the team, coming together and understanding what it takes to win games. ... Tonight was just a culmination of everything," Falcons head coach Tim Caffey said. "The kids wanted it. They waited 365 days for this." Amid rough weather and field conditions, it didn't appear either side would crack the scoreboard, but the home team got on the board right before halftime. Junior quarterback Dre Lott found fellow junior Gage Wilson on a fade pattern for a 7-yard touchdown pass, completing a 13-play, 84-yard drive with 5.2 seconds left in the second quarter. As the rain picked up, the game snowballed from there. After forcing a Martin County three-and-out, the Falcons (8-2) struck on their first offensive play of the second half as Alex Thornton burst through the line of scrimmage, bounced outside and outran the defense for a 51-yard touchdown run. item.title: Ja Morant’s Hamstring Blow Kills Portland’s Early Hopes Immediately
item.description: Troy Wayrynen-Imagn Images Ja Morant will miss at least four weeks after suffering a Grade 2 left hamstring strain in Thursday’s loss to the Grizzlies, according to the New York Post . The Portland Trail Blazers confirmed the injury on Friday, ending his early-season run before it truly started. This setback comes just one week into the NBA regular season and leaves the team without its leading scorer. Morant played 23 minutes before exiting with 7:46 left in the game. He finished with 14 points and three assists against his former club. The timing is brutal for a franchise trying to find its footing. Morant was averaging 15.8 points and 5.5 assists through the first four games. He shot a career-best 42.9 percent from three-point range, a stat that now looks like a fleeting high point. The Blazers confirmed he will be re-evaluated in four weeks. That timeline means he likely returns in late November or early December. Portland now faces a long stretch without its best player while trying to build momentum. A Pattern of Broken Bodies This injury is not an isolated incident for the 27-year-old guard. Morant has missed significant time due to injuries and suspensions over the last three seasons. He played just 79 games in his final three years with Memphis. Last season, he appeared in 20 games and averaged 19.5 points. His availability has been a major issue for the Grizzlies before they traded him. The move to Portland came with a five-year, $197 million extension signed in 2022. Now that deal looks even riskier with another major injury on the ledger. item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Most fans expect a new head coach to bring strict discipline or loud sideline commands, but veteran safety Jessie Bates III says the biggest change in Atlanta is actually quiet. The Falcons are riding high after a 29-20 win over the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, Oct. 25, yet the team culture has shifted in a way that defies the usual NFL script. Bates told the Pat McAfee Show that the leadership style of Kevin Stefanski and Michael Penix Jr. relies on a steady presence rather than noise. item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Philadelphia 76ers are not just hoping to win this season. They are built to dominate, thanks to a front office that moved faster than anyone expected. Mike Gansey, the new team president, orchestrated a summer of trades and signings that has the entire league talking. Then he led the push to secure LeBron James for the franchise. The Sixer Sense reported that he also signed Dean Wade and brought in Anfernee Simons on a great contract. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope joined the mix after being recruited from Memphis. These are not small tweaks. They are major shifts that extend the championship window for years to come. But the scale of what Gansey did changes the conversation. The Sixers added superstars and depth in one go. The talent on the roster is now unmatched in the league. Fans and experts alike are already calling his body of work historic. Validation for LeBron James LeBron James had choices this summer. He could have stayed with the Cavaliers, joined the Heat, or gone to the Warriors. He chose Philadelphia because he wants a fifth title. The Sixers are 4-1 so far, including a win over the Knicks and a comeback victory against Cleveland. Tyrese Maxey is playing like an early MVP candidate, which was a key reason James signed. The Sixer Sense noted that James did not have to carry the team alone on Wednesday. He scored 20.6 points per game and grabbed 10 rebounds in a recent win against Indiana. The team still has work to do. They need a backup big man after Ariel Hukporti suffered a torn Achilles. But the core is strong. The roster construction gives James the best shot at winning. He made a smart choice, and the front office proved it by building around him. The season is young, but the path to a title looks clear. The Verdict on Gansey Mike Gansey has done what no other executive has done in recent memory. He fixed the roster, added stars, and set the team up for the future. item.title: Jeffery Simmons reveals what Bears trade told him after emotional Titans departure
item.description: Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images Jeffery Simmons has opened up about his emotional departure from the Tennessee Titans after being traded to the Chicago Bears, admitting the move told him everything he needed to know about his new team. The defensive tackle spent eight seasons in Nashville after being selected 19th overall in the 2019 NFL Draft. During that time, he earned four Pro Bowl selections and three All-Pro honours. Simmons now joins a Bears team that is 5-2 heading into Week 8 and looking to make a push towards the playoffs. Jeffery Simmons says Chicago Bears trade showed the team wants to win now Simmons did not hide how difficult the trade had been when speaking to reporters after beginning practice with Chicago. “Man, I tell you, yesterday was pretty hard,” Simmons said. “I’m excited to be a Chicago Bear.” However, the move also gave Simmons a clear message about the Bears’ ambitions. “The trade told me everything I needed to know… This team believes in what they have here and they want it now.” Chicago’s record suggests Simmons is joining a team with genuine postseason ambitions. His arrival could prove significant as the Bears look to strengthen their defence for the remainder of the campaign. Before leaving Tennessee, Simmons had established himself as one of the franchise’s most important players. Across 106 appearances for the Titans, he recorded 46.5 sacks, 414 tackles, 31 pass deflections and nine forced fumbles. He also agreed to a three-year, $105.8 million contract before the trade, making him one of the highest-paid players at his position. Despite the opportunity in Chicago, Simmons made it clear that leaving Nashville was not an easy decision. In a heartfelt farewell message, he explained how much the city and its supporters had meant to him throughout his career. “Nashville became home,” Simmons wrote, adding that he had always imagined finishing what he started with the Titans and helping bring winning football back to the organisation. He also thanked Titans fans for supporting his family and foundation throughout his time with the team. Simmons’ focus now shifts to his new surroundings, with the Bears potentially handing him his debut against the Seattle Seahawks. His arrival gives Chicago an experienced defensive presence as it looks to maintain its strong start and push towards the playoffs.
